director.chapterArc: An apparently ordinary northward journey reveals Rook's physical decline, then converts roadside sociability into proof of surveillance. His deductions narrow the landscape into a deliberate trap; the Level offers defensible geometry but no escape. Hoyle's calm ultimatum turns Rook's surrender into a measurable price for everyone else's safety, and the chapter closes with nine fires confirming that the promised violence is already in position.
director.restraintNote: Keep Original Calder grounded and observant. Let dread emerge through arithmetic, altered routines, cold hands, road geometry, and ordinary voices rather than overt menace. Rook's admissions carry fatigue and loss of tactical identity without self-pity; Hoyle remains courteous and procedural. Humor should stay dry and briefly human, making its disappearance after the scouts more consequential.

cues.delivery: Give Milo's self-valuation an open, reflexive brightness; let the joke expose how little he understands the correction coming.
cues.from: Behind them Milo said, cheerfully, "I'm worth a great deal."
cues.through: Behind them Milo said, cheerfully, "I'm worth a great deal."
cues.reason: A brief comic beat establishes the warmth that Dessa immediately removes.

cues.delivery: Dessa's rebuke is protective, not cross: firm the rhythm and let concern appear only in her refusal to permit comforting fiction.
cues.from: "You're worth more than he is at the minute," said Dessa, "and that's not a joke, and I'd like you to stop making it into one before somebody needs it not to be."
cues.through: "You're worth more than he is at the minute," said Dessa, "and that's not a joke, and I'd like you to stop making it into one before somebody needs it not to be."
cues.reason: Her severity is an act of preparation and care.

cues.delivery: Play the exchange as dry road-worn banter. Rook is deliberately spending wit to lighten the halt, never performing for applause.
cues.from: "Is there a wall between here and Meridian?" he said, with his mouth full. "An actual one, with a gate and a weighmaster and a person who sells things."
cues.through: "They sell it to people who want flax," said Rook, "which as far as I can tell is nobody, which is why it's still there, because nobody's ever wanted anything they have enough to come and take it. Ferrow is the safest settlement in this country and it is the dullest place on the face of the earth and every single person in it is ninety."
cues.reason: This is the chapter's last sustained ease before Rook states his decline.

cues.delivery: Keep Toren's fear cool and bodily—a steady pressure with nowhere to discharge, not a surge of alarm.
cues.from: Nobody said anything. He had done it four times in three days and he had started doing it in front of them instead of up a bank, and Toren had begun to be frightened of it in a low steady way that did not have anywhere to go.
cues.through: Nobody said anything. He had done it four times in three days and he had started doing it in front of them instead of up a bank, and Toren had begun to be frightened of it in a low steady way that did not have anywhere to go.
cues.reason: The repeated pulse-check has become a private omen.

cues.delivery: Rook itemizes his diminishing usefulness with exact, unembellished clarity. Allow the loss beneath the arithmetic, but no plea, bitterness, or farewell cadence.
cues.from: "I did," said Rook. "And last night I sat in a cart bed for three quarters of an hour with my hands on an old woman's chest, and that's where the difference went, and it will go there again tonight and tomorrow night and every night after, because that's what it's for." He screwed the cap of the empty flask down, which he did about nine times a day now, a thing his hands did without him. "I'd like everybody to understand the shape of it rather than the number, because the number's going to keep doing that. I fill fast. I fill faster than any of you and it's not a skill and I've explained why. What I haven't got is anything put by. The flask was nine days of me in a tin and I poured it into a cup, and what that means is that from now until I stop, I am carrying exactly as much as I have made since the morning, and every night I give it to her.
cues.through: "So: a tenth. Which is a man who can hold the stone, put an edge on it, and walk about. It is not a man who can put up a shape that'll stop anything, and it is not a man who can cross forty feet of road faster than you can look at it, and if any of you are carrying a picture of me doing either of those things this week, take it out and burn it now, this afternoon, while it's cheap."
cues.reason: He dismantles the group's image of him and acknowledges his approaching obsolescence.

cues.delivery: Land the image of the ordinary corpse as flat gallows humor; the joke is a tool for making the forecast usable.
cues.from: "Then you'll have burnt it already," said Rook, "and you'll thank me, and I won't hear you, because I'll be dead in a ditch with a knife in my hand looking extremely ordinary."
cues.through: "Then you'll have burnt it already," said Rook, "and you'll thank me, and I won't hear you, because I'll be dead in a ditch with a knife in my hand looking extremely ordinary."
cues.reason: Rook converts the possibility of his death into a practical correction.

cues.delivery: Let Senna's answer and the boys' easy exchange breathe with modest warmth. Keep it commonplace—the later betrayal depends on its innocence.
cues.from: "I've picked a poor decade for it," said Senna.
cues.through: The man laughed. The young one laughed too, a beat late, and looked at Milo, and Milo — who could not help it, who had never once been able to help it — offered him the last of the bread out of the cloth, and the boy took it and said "ta," and ate it in three bites like somebody who had walked a long way, and Milo asked him if the road south was any good, and the boy said it was a road, and Milo said that was the trouble with roads, and the two of them stood there in the middle of the afternoon for a minute and a half grinning at each other about nothing.
cues.reason: Ordinary fellowship disguises the scouts' work and makes the bread consequential.

cues.delivery: State Rook's identification without flourish, then register the effect through Toren's cold hands. The shock is recognition, not panic.
cues.from: "That was them."
cues.through: Nobody said anything at all for about three seconds, and Toren discovered that his hands had gone cold in a way they did not go cold for husks.
cues.reason: The harmless travelers are reclassified as scouts.

cues.delivery: Keep the explanation surgical, but soften only on Rook's acknowledgment of Toren: approval offered as usable fact, not reassurance.
cues.from: "Because a man who tells you he's hunting somebody isn't hunting you," said Rook. "That's the whole of it. It costs him nothing, it makes him a chancer after a bounty instead of a scout, and it means that if any of you had seen me, one of you would have said so, and the one who'd have said so is thirteen and has a face like a window." He looked at Toren. "You did well. You said nothing. You said nothing because you'd gone cold and couldn't think of anything, and I'll take it."
cues.through: "Because a man who tells you he's hunting somebody isn't hunting you," said Rook. "That's the whole of it. It costs him nothing, it makes him a chancer after a bounty instead of a scout, and it means that if any of you had seen me, one of you would have said so, and the one who'd have said so is thirteen and has a face like a window." He looked at Toren. "You did well. You said nothing. You said nothing because you'd gone cold and couldn't think of anything, and I'll take it."
cues.reason: Rook recognizes Toren's accidental silence as competent survival.

cues.delivery: Let Milo's broken repetition carry shame through the missing end of the sentence. Stay small and disbelieving; do not solicit sympathy.
cues.from: "He ate the bread," Milo said.
cues.through: "I gave him the bread and he stood there and laughed at—"
cues.reason: The shared bread has become evidence that Milo helped an enemy.

cues.delivery: Rook protects Milo by turning mercy into arithmetic. Be firm on the absolution and warmer only underneath the insistence that generosity must survive.
cues.from: "Yes," said Rook. "And he's seventeen and he's had a joining fee in brass in his pocket for about eleven days and he has not yet worked out what he's joined, and when he does it'll be in the dark with somebody shouting at him. That one's not a liar. He's a boy who's been put next to a liar and told to walk south looking pleased." He took his hand off the rail. "Milo. Look at me. You did not do anything wrong and you are not going to start being careful about handing people bread, because if that ever goes out of you the rest of us are finished. That's not comfort, it's the arithmetic. Now go and sit up with your grandmother, because the next bit is going to be unpleasant and I want you where she can get hold of you."
cues.through: "Yes," said Rook. "And he's seventeen and he's had a joining fee in brass in his pocket for about eleven days and he has not yet worked out what he's joined, and when he does it'll be in the dark with somebody shouting at him. That one's not a liar. He's a boy who's been put next to a liar and told to walk south looking pleased." He took his hand off the rail. "Milo. Look at me. You did not do anything wrong and you are not going to start being careful about handing people bread, because if that ever goes out of you the rest of us are finished. That's not comfort, it's the arithmetic. Now go and sit up with your grandmother, because the next bit is going to be unpleasant and I want you where she can get hold of you."
cues.reason: Rook prevents Milo's guilt from hardening into permanent suspicion.

cues.delivery: Deliver the chain of cause and responsibility as a ledger entry. Rook claims the cost without blaming Ott or asking forgiveness.
cues.from: "Because a woman walked into that yard with better ash than anybody's seen out of that country in a year and sold it well," said Rook, "and somebody at that table asked her where a salvager gets road-ash of that grade, and she told a story that didn't have me in it, and it had me in it anyway, because there is one man on this road who pours out half a flask to pay for apples and I have been doing it in ninety settlements for six years." He put the stick down. "That's not Ott's fault and nobody is going to say one word against Ott at any fire on this road. That's mine. I have spent six years making a shape in this country that could be recognized, and it got recognized, and the first time it has ever cost anybody anything it's going to cost all of you."

cues.reason: His six-year reputation is revealed as the mechanism endangering the group.

cues.delivery: Let Rook mourn the loss of choosing ground solely through controlled tactical explanation. Hold every spatial relation clear; resignation must never blur the plan.
cues.from: "And I'd like everybody to hear the next part properly," he said, "because it's the thing I have been dreading for a fortnight and it's arrived and I'd rather say it than have you all watch me not say it.
cues.through: "So that's where we're going. Up onto it, tonight, because the alternative is to sit in a wet field in the open with two of them behind us counting, and I will take a bad road I can only be come at from two ends over good country I can be come at from everywhere."
cues.reason: He names the collapse of the one advantage on which his identity and survival depended.

cues.delivery: Widen the cadence for the enormous water and sky, but make the scale exposing rather than beautiful. End on the absence of cover.
cues.from: It came up out of the grazing slowly — the road lifting, the hedges dropping away and stopping altogether, and then suddenly there was nothing on either side of the ruts but a long dark grass slope going down twelve or fourteen feet to water, and the water going out flat and pale and enormous in both directions under the evening with the reed beds standing black in it in long combed streaks.
cues.through: It was the widest sky Toren had ever stood under. It had not one single thing in it to stand behind.
cues.reason: The landscape physically reveals the trap's magnitude.

cues.delivery: Give Hoyle the calm patience of a practiced negotiator. Enumerate the terms evenly; the threat gains force from precision and his lack of emotional investment.
cues.from: "Hoyle," he said. "I'm the one they send. My name's not worth anything and I'll give it you anyway, because you'll hear it later and I'd rather you'd had it from me." He turned his palms a little further out. "Four terms, and I'll say them once and slowly, and then I'll go away and you can talk about it all night, which is what you're going to do anyway.
cues.through: "Four." He let his hands fall to his sides. "If he doesn't come out, then in about a day and a half we'll do it the other way, and the other way is twenty-odd men on eleven miles of raised road with a cart on it, and I have got nowhere else to be until it's finished. I'm not saying that to frighten the children. I'm saying it because you'll do the sum yourselves in an hour and I'd rather you had my numbers than your own."
cues.reason: The surrender offer prices every vulnerability and makes the alternative mathematically inevitable.

cues.delivery: Keep Hoyle's account matter-of-fact and Rook's interruption almost casual. Let the final recognition land through stillness: Rook was identified because he alone never reacted.
cues.from: "Fair," he said. "Then I'll tell you the true one for nothing, since we're being plain. He's been in the same country as us for six years buying our chits and asking after us at every wall between here and the coast, and a man does not do that for six years over a debt. Whatever's between him and my section is old and it's deep and none of you were born for it. That's all I know and it's all I want to know, and I've been in this trade twenty-two years, and I'd say the same about him if he was standing here and I was in the cart."
cues.through: "I know," said Hoyle. "I've known since I came up the road. You're the only one who hasn't moved."
cues.reason: The old pursuit becomes mutual recognition in the dark.

cues.delivery: Narrow Dessa's second report as the first crack in her sensor's certainty. Keep the words exact and audible; the fear lies in how nearly the hidden watcher escaped her.
cues.from: He went back down the road and the dark took him and Dessa tracked him out to thirty feet and said, "Gone," and then said, a moment later, in a much smaller voice, "There's another one at the edge. There's another one at the edge and I only got him because he moved."
cues.through: He went back down the road and the dark took him and Dessa tracked him out to thirty feet and said, "Gone," and then said, a moment later, in a much smaller voice, "There's another one at the edge. There's another one at the edge and I only got him because he moved."
cues.reason: A second concealed observer proves the negotiation itself was covered.

cues.delivery: Warm only the physical contact. Senna offers weight and presence instead of reassurance, and Toren receives it without naming what it means.
cues.from: Toren went and sat on the tailgate near his grandmother because it was the only place on eleven miles of raised road that had a wall to it, and after a while Senna put her good hand flat on his back between the shoulder blades and left it there, and did not say one word about any of it, which he was grateful for in a way he could not have said out loud.
cues.through: Toren went and sat on the tailgate near his grandmother because it was the only place on eleven miles of raised road that had a wall to it, and after a while Senna put her good hand flat on his back between the shoulder blades and left it there, and did not say one word about any of it, which he was grateful for in a way he could not have said out loud.
cues.reason: The silent hand on Toren's back is the chapter's restrained emotional shelter.

cues.delivery: Let Milo reason in a tight, troubled cadence, circling the prepared offer rather than raising his voice. His fear is that their deepest need was observed and weaponized.
cues.from: "He said he'd give her four days," Milo said.
cues.through: "I'm not — I know. I'm not saying we should." He picked at the rag on his thumb. "I'm saying he knew to say it. That's what I can't get past. He came up that road and the first thing he had in his mouth was the exact thing we most want in the world and he'd got it ready, and he'd got it ready because somebody stood in the road this afternoon and looked in the cart bed."
cues.reason: The ash offer reveals the hunters' surveillance and tactical understanding.

cues.delivery: Count the distant lights with measured visual precision. Do not enlarge them; nine small, stationary facts are enough.
cues.from: They were down there on the road, a long way back, where the embankment came up out of the grazing — small orange points in a loose line across the width of the bank and a little way down the slope on both sides. Toren counted them twice and got nine both times.
cues.through: They were down there on the road, a long way back, where the embankment came up out of the grazing — small orange points in a loose line across the width of the bank and a little way down the slope on both sides. Toren counted them twice and got nine both times.
cues.reason: The fires turn the abstract force into a visible deployment.
